cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The Commonwealth is a voluntary association of 56 independent countries with a combined population of 2.5 billion people, most with historic ties to Britain through the former British Empire.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The Commonwealth promotes shared values: democracy, human rights, the rule of law, and sustainable development. The Commonwealth Charter sets out these principles, but membership is voluntary and enforcement is limited.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: Commonwealth Heads of Government Meetings (CHOGM) are held every two years to discuss shared challenges and set the organisation's direction. The King is the Head of the Commonwealth.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The United Nations (UN) was founded in 1945 to maintain international peace, develop friendly relations, and promote human rights. It has 193 member states.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The UN Security Council has 5 permanent members (UK, US, France, Russia, China) with veto power. This veto often prevents action when permanent members disagree, e.g. on Syria and Ukraine.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: NATO is a military alliance of 32 countries committed to collective defence under Article 5 — an attack on one is an attack on all. The UK is a founding member.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The Council of Europe (NOT the EU) oversees the European Convention on Human Rights and the European Court of Human Rights. The UK remains a member post-Brexit.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The WTO sets and enforces rules for international trade and resolves trade disputes between member states. All members must follow the same trade rules.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The International Criminal Court (ICC) prosecutes individuals for genocide, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and aggression. The UK is a member but not all countries recognise its jurisdiction.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: International organisations can limit national sovereignty by requiring members to follow shared rules and accept joint decisions. This is a key tension in international cooperation.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The UK contributes financially and militarily to many international organisations, but the level of contribution and commitment is subject to political debate.

cards.front: Recall a key point about The Commonwealth & International Organisations
cards.back: The effectiveness of international organisations depends on the willingness of member states to cooperate and enforce decisions — without enforcement powers, they rely on consensus and persuasion.

cards.front: What should you know about citizenship studies exam tips — the commonwealth & international organisations?
cards.back: 1. For The Commonwealth & International Organisations questions, use citizenship terminology and reference democratic processes accurately 2. Consider multiple viewpoints — including those you disagree with 3. Link The Commonwealth & International Organisations to current affairs and real-world examples where possible 4. When evaluating, consider both rights and responsibilities 5. Structure longer answers: identify the issue, analyse different perspectives, reach a justified view
